description: A D_PDU whose header completes in the block after the one holding its first byte counts its EOT from that first block, plus the byte's share of it rounded up.
note: Conn 1 binds SAP 5 for non-ARQ and gets S_BIND_ACCEPTED (A-0041, A-0047). Every received D_PDU is a single-segment NON-ARQ-DATA (type 7, address size 4, C_PDU ID as stated, reception window 20) from 0.0.1.3 to 0.0.1.9 whose segment is a DATA C_PDU holding a DATA S_PDU from SAP 9 to SAP 9 with U_PDU "hi" (31 bytes, as in dts-rx-vdcd-end-after-burst-end). burst_started gives block_ms (corpus 0.31.0), so each EOT counts from the latest instant its D_PDU can have started on air: the arrival time of the bytes_received holding its first byte, less block_ms, plus ceil(offset x block_ms / bytes in that bytes_received) (interp C-1289); the burst's estimate is the earliest end time (C-0843). After the burst, conn 1's S_UNIDATA_REQUEST (priority 0 to SAP 5 at 0.0.1.3, U_PDU "hello", no confirmation) is queued: no SIS output (A-0095, K-0096), dts.ttd starts at its TTD (C-1050), and with the channel busy until the estimate csma.vdcd_end runs to it (K-0073, K-0111). At its expiry VDCD clears last and the D_PDUs heard were addressed to another node, so rule 3 gives lbt_wait_vdcd_ms 3000 (K-0071, K-0073). burst_started at 1000 gives block_ms 1000. The block at 2100 holds 11 zero bytes and the first 10 bytes of D_PDU A (C_PDU ID 1, EOT 5); the block at 3100 holds its other 21 bytes, completing its header and data (C-0973, D-0007). Its first byte is at offset 11 of the 21-byte block that arrived at 2100: anchor 2100 - 1000 + ceil(11 x 1000 / 21) = 1100 + 524 = 1624, end 1624 + 2500 = 4124 (C-1289), against 3100 + 2500 = 5600 under C-1024 alone. The burst ends at 3200 (eom, 2 blocks) with nothing queued, so no output. The request at 3300 starts dts.ttd and csma.vdcd_end 824 ms; at 4124 rule 3 gives csma.lbt_wait 3000.
